Source format: Recall notice

WarmGlow Pty Ltd has received three reports of heaters continuing to emit heat after the unit was switched off, and one report of a strong gas odour emanating from the appliance during the off cycle. No injuries have been reported to date.

The fault has been traced to a defective thermocouple assembly supplied by a component manufacturer. The thermocouple may fail to detect the pilot flame, leaving the gas valve open. The affected component was fitted to units manufactured between October 2022 and March 2023.

---

**3. HAZARD IDENTIFIED**

- Fire hazard
- Explosion hazard due to gas accumulation

Consumers are advised that the hazard may occur without warning and is not dependent on the age of the unit or the frequency of use.

---

**4. DATES AND IDENTIFICATION OF THE DEFECT**

The defect was identified during routine internal quality assurance testing in April 2024. WarmGlow Pty Ltd notified the Commission on 20 May 2024. This recall notice is issued following consultation with the Commission and agreement on the proposed remedy.

The defect is not present in units manufactured after March 2023. Units with batch codes earlier than November 2022 are not affected.

---

**5. REMEDY**

Consumers who have purchased an affected unit should stop using the heater immediately and switch off the gas supply at the isolation valve, if it is safe to do so. Do not attempt to disconnect the heater yourself.

WarmGlow Pty Ltd will arrange for a qualified technician to attend the consumer's premises at no cost to:

- Replace the thermocouple assembly with a corrected component; and
- Test the gas valve operation to confirm safe function.

Where the unit cannot be repaired on site, WarmGlow Pty Ltd will arrange for collection of the heater and supply a replacement unit of equivalent value. All costs associated with the remedy, including travel, parts, and labour, will be borne by WarmGlow Pty Ltd.

WarmGlow Pty Ltd issued recall notice WarmGlow Recall Notice 2024-03. Record status: current.

Consumers are not entitled to a refund under this recall. The remedy is limited to repair or replacement as described above.

---

**6. WHAT CONSUMERS SHOULD DO**

1. Locate the batch code on the rating plate on the rear lower panel of the heater.
2. If the batch code is listed in Section 1 of this notice, immediately stop using the heater and turn off the gas supply at the wall isolation valve.
3. Contact WarmGlow Pty Ltd to register for the free repair or replacement.

Contact details:

- **Telephone:** 1800 555 019 (free call, Monday to Friday, 8:30 am to 5:00 pm AEST)
- **Email:** recall@warmglow.com.au
- **Web:** www.warmglow.com.au/recall-2024-03

When contacting WarmGlow, please have the following information available:

- Batch code from the rating plate
- Date of purchase, if known
- Retailer where the unit was purchased, if known

WarmGlow Pty Ltd will arrange an appointment with a licensed gas fitter in the consumer's area. Appointments will be scheduled within 20 business days of registration.

---

**7. RETAILERS AND SUPPLIERS**

Retailers who have sold affected units should:

- Remove any remaining affected stock from sale immediately.
- Contact WarmGlow Pty Ltd to arrange return or on-site rectification of affected stock.
- Display a copy of this recall notice at the point of sale for a period of 60 days from the date of issue.
- Provide a copy of this notice to any consumer who purchased an affected unit from their store, where the retailer holds contact details.

A list of known retailers who received affected stock is available from WarmGlow Pty Ltd on request.

---
*Correction note:* An earlier version of this notice (dated 05/06/2024, revision A) listed 14,200 affected units. That figure included units manufactured in February 2024 that have since been confirmed as unaffected following further testing. The correct figure is 12,500 units. This notice (revision B) supersedes revision A.

**Retailers:** Affected stock was supplied to the following retailers:

- HomePlus Bayside

- WarmGlow Factory Outlet (Homebush)
- Independent stockists listed in the retailer schedule available from WarmGlow Pty Ltd on request

**Units not affected:** WarmGlow Model WG-2400 heaters with batch codes commencing 2402 or earlier, and units with batch codes commencing 2406 or later, are not affected by this recall. Units with batch codes in the ranges listed above are affected regardless of the date of purchase or installation.

Testing identified a fault in the thermocouple assembly in affected units. The thermocouple may fail to detect the presence of a flame, allowing the gas supply to continue after the flame has been extinguished. This presents a risk of gas accumulation and a potential fire or explosion hazard.

The fault is present in units manufactured during the production periods listed in Section 1. WarmGlow Pty Ltd became aware of the issue following a consumer report received on 22/05/2024 and confirmed the fault through internal testing completed on 03/06/2024.

**6.1 What you can choose**

Under the terms of this recall, you may choose either of the following remedies, at no cost to you:

- **Repair** – A qualified WarmGlow technician will replace the thermocouple assembly in your heater and carry out a functional test. The repair can be done in your home for most installations. If the heater cannot be repaired on site, WarmGlow will arrange collection and return it to you once the repair is complete.
- **Replacement** – If you prefer not to have the heater repaired, or if the unit cannot be safely repaired, WarmGlow will supply a replacement heater of equivalent value. The replacement model currently offered is the WarmGlow Model WG-2600, which has the same heating capacity and safety features. If the WG-2600 is not suitable for your needs, please contact WarmGlow to discuss alternatives.

**Important:** A refund is not available under this recall. The remedy is limited to repair or replacement as described above. This does not affect any rights you may have under the Australian Consumer Law.

**6.2 How to register for a remedy**

To arrange your remedy, you must register your heater with WarmGlow Pty Ltd. Registration is quick and can be done in one of three ways:

1. **Online** – Visit our recall registration page at www.warmglow.com.au/recall2024 and complete the online form. You will need your heater's model number (WG-2400) and batch code, which are printed on the rating label on the back of the unit.
2. **By phone** – Call our recall hotline on **1800 555 047** between 8:30 am and 5:00 pm (AEST), Monday to Friday. Our staff will take your details over the phone and book an appointment for you.
3. **By email** – Send an email to recall@warmglow.com.au with your name, contact number, address, and the batch code from your heater's rating label. We will respond within two business days.

**6.3 What happens after you register**

Once you have registered, WarmGlow will contact you to arrange a suitable time for the remedy. Please note the following:

- Appointments are scheduled within 20 business days of registration. As at the date of this notice, the average waiting time for an appointment is 16 business days.
- For repairs in the home, our technician will bring the replacement thermocouple assembly and all necessary tools. The repair takes approximately 30 minutes.
- If your heater needs to be collected for repair, WarmGlow will arrange a courier to pick it up from your address. The heater will be returned to you within 10 business days of collection.
- For replacements, the new heater will be delivered to your address. Our courier will take the old heater away at the time of delivery.

**6.4 Preparing for your appointment**

To help our technician complete the repair as quickly as possible, please:

- Make sure the heater is unplugged and cool before the technician arrives.
- Clear a space around the heater so the technician can access all sides of the unit.
- Have the heater's rating label visible if possible, so the technician can confirm the batch code.

**6.5 If you have already had the heater repaired**

If you have already had your heater repaired by a technician who was not authorised by WarmGlow, you may still be eligible for a remedy. Please contact the recall hotline and have your repair receipt available. We will assess each case individually.

WarmGlow will arrange for the repair or replacement to be carried out at the address you provide. If you have already registered and have since moved, please contact the recall hotline or email recall@warmglow.com.au with your updated details so we can ensure our records are correct.

---

**7. Where to find more information**

For further information about this recall, including the full list of affected batch codes, please visit the Product Safety Australia website at **www.productsafety.gov.au** and search for recall number **2024/12345**. The listing includes a copy of this notice, photographs of the affected heater model, and the full list of batch codes.

You can also find more information on the WarmGlow website at **www.warmglow.com.au/recall**. This page includes:

- A copy of this notice and any future revisions
- A list of frequently asked questions
- A short video showing how to locate the rating label on your heater
- A downloadable form you can print and post to us if you prefer not to register online, by phone, or by email

If you have any questions that are not answered by the information on these websites, please call the recall hotline on **1800 555 047** or send an email to **recall@warmglow.com.au**.

---

If you would like to receive updates about this recall by email or SMS, you can register for updates at **www.warmglow.com.au/recall/updates**. When you register for updates, we will send you:

- A confirmation when your remedy has been scheduled
- A reminder the day before your appointment
- A notification if there are any changes to the recall, such as an extension of the affected batch range or a change to the remedy

Please note that registering for updates is separate from registering your heater for the remedy. Recall Notice 2024/12345 (Revision 3)
Issued 19 June 2024

**WarmGlow Ceramic Fan Heater — Model GHG-2000**
**Recall number: 2024/12345**
**Revision 3 — supersedes Revision 2 dated 12 June 2024**

This revision is issued to update the contact details for the remedy provider in Western Australia and to clarify the compliance status of replacement thermocouples used in repaired units. All other terms of the recall remain unchanged.

---

**1. Product description**

The recall affects the WarmGlow Ceramic Fan Heater, model GHG-2000, with a nominal power rating of 2000 W and a rated voltage of 220–240 V AC. The heater is a freestanding, fan-forced ceramic heater with a white body and a black control panel on the top rear of the unit. The model number and batch code are printed on the silver rating label affixed to the underside of the base.

Affected batch codes are:

GHG-2000-2301 through GHG-2000-2311 inclusive, and
GHG-2000-2401 through GHG-2000-2404 inclusive.

The batch code is a nine-character code printed on the rating label, for example, GHG-2000-2307. Only units with a batch code within the ranges listed above are affected. Units with a batch code outside these ranges are not affected by this recall.

Approximately 12,400 units with affected batch codes were sold in Australia between 1 January 2023 and 31 May 2024. The heaters were sold through major retailers including HomePlus Bayside, Coastal Electrical, and a number of independent hardware and home appliance stores, as well as through online marketplaces.

**2. Reason for the recall**

The heater has been found to present a risk of fire and burn injury due to a manufacturing defect in the thermal cutoff device. In affected units, the thermal cutoff may fail to operate correctly, allowing the heater to continue operating when the internal temperature exceeds the designed safe limit. This can cause the heater body to overheat, potentially resulting in the plastic housing melting or catching fire.

The defect was identified following a consumer incident reported to WarmGlow on 22 April 2024, in which a heater in a residential property in Bayside began to emit smoke and the rear panel showed signs of melting. The unit was returned to WarmGlow for examination, and testing confirmed that the thermal cutoff device had not activated at the required temperature. Subsequent testing of a sample of units from the same production batch identified the fault in a small proportion of units. The supplier of the thermal cutoff device has advised that a change in the calibration procedure at their factory in March 2023 may have resulted in a batch of devices with an incorrectly set trip temperature.

WarmGlow has received two further reports of heaters overheating, one in May 2024 and one in early June 2024. No injuries have been reported. The recall is being conducted in consultation with the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (the Commission).

**3. Hazards**

The main hazard associated with the affected heaters is fire. If the thermal cutoff device fails to operate, the heater can continue to heat beyond its design limits. The external surfaces of the heater can reach temperatures high enough to ignite nearby combustible materials or to cause burn injuries if touched. The heater may also emit smoke and an odour of burning plastic before the housing begins to melt.

Consumers are advised to stop using the heater immediately, unplug it from the power outlet, and not to use the heater again until it has been inspected and, if necessary, repaired or replaced under this recall.
**4. What consumers should do**

Consumers who have purchased one of the affected WarmGlow WG-2000 panel heaters should immediately stop using the heater, unplug it from the power outlet, and contact WarmGlow to arrange a free replacement or refund.

To arrange a remedy, consumers can:

- Call WarmGlow’s dedicated recall hotline on 1800 634 227 (Monday to Friday, 9:00 am to 5:00 pm AEST).
- Email the recall team at recall@warmglow.com.au.
- Visit the WarmGlow website at www.warmglow.com.au/recall and complete the online recall form.

Consumers will need to provide their name, contact details, the model number and serial number from the rating label on the back of the heater, and proof of purchase if available. Proof of purchase is not required to receive a remedy, but it will help WarmGlow confirm the date and place of purchase.

WarmGlow will arrange for the affected heater to be collected from the consumer’s home at no cost, or will provide a prepaid return satchel for smaller items where collection is not practicable. Once the heater has been received and verified as an affected unit, WarmGlow will issue either a replacement heater of equivalent value or a full refund of the purchase price, at the consumer’s choice.

Consumers who purchased their heater from a retail store and prefer to return it in person may do so at the point of purchase. Participating retailers have been advised of the recall and will accept affected units. Consumers returning a heater to a store should bring their receipt if available, but the absence of a receipt will not prevent the return being processed.

Consumers who have registered their heater with WarmGlow for warranty purposes have been contacted directly by email or post with details of the recall. If you have not received a notification but believe your heater may be affected, please check the model and serial number against the list on the WarmGlow website or contact the recall hotline for assistance.

**5. Affected products and identification**

The recall affects the following product:

- Brand: WarmGlow
- Model: WG-2000
- Description: 2000W panel heater with digital thermostat, white finish
- Batch codes: 2023-03-01 through 2023-03-31 inclusive
- Serial number range: WG2000-30123-000001 through WG2000-30123-004800

The affected batch codes and serial number range are printed on the rating label located on the rear panel of the heater, near the power cord. The batch code is formatted as a date in the sequence YYYY-MM-DD. Consumers who have difficulty reading the rating label due to the position of the heater are advised to unplug the unit and, if necessary, lay it face down on a soft surface before attempting to read the label.

Units manufactured outside the batch code range listed above are not affected by this recall. Consumers who are unsure whether their unit is affected should contact the recall hotline for assistance, providing the batch code and serial number from the rating label.

**6. Remedy**

WarmGlow will provide a free replacement heater or a full refund of the purchase price for all affected units, regardless of the age of the heater and regardless of whether the consumer has proof of purchase. The consumer may choose which remedy they prefer. Replacement units are of the same model and specification, and have been manufactured with a corrected thermal cutoff device from a different supplier. The replacement units do not carry the defect described in this recall notice.

WarmGlow Pty Ltd has received three reports of heaters continuing to emit heat after the unit was switched off, and one report of a strong gas odour emanating from the appliance during the off cycle. No injuries have been reported to date.

The fault has been traced to a defective thermocouple assembly supplied by a component manufacturer. The thermocouple may fail to detect the pilot flame, leaving the gas valve open. The affected component was fitted to units manufactured between October 2022 and March 2023.

---

**3. HAZARD IDENTIFIED**

- Fire hazard
- Explosion hazard due to gas accumulation

Consumers are advised that the hazard may occur without warning and is not dependent on the age of the unit or the frequency of use.

---

**4. DATES AND IDENTIFICATION OF THE DEFECT**

The defect was identified during routine internal quality assurance testing in April 2024. WarmGlow Pty Ltd notified the Commission on 20 May 2024. This recall notice is issued following consultation with the Commission and agreement on the proposed remedy.

The defect is not present in units manufactured after March 2023. Units with batch codes earlier than November 2022 are not affected.

---

**5. REMEDY**

Consumers who have purchased an affected unit should stop using the heater immediately and switch off the gas supply at the isolation valve, if it is safe to do so. Do not attempt to disconnect the heater yourself.

WarmGlow Pty Ltd will arrange for a qualified technician to attend the consumer's premises at no cost to:

- Replace the thermocouple assembly with a corrected component; and
- Test the gas valve operation to confirm safe function.

Where the unit cannot be repaired on site, WarmGlow Pty Ltd will arrange for collection of the heater and supply a replacement unit of equivalent value. All costs associated with the remedy, including travel, parts, and labour, will be borne by WarmGlow Pty Ltd.

WarmGlow Pty Ltd issued recall notice WarmGlow Recall Notice 2024-03. Record status: current.

Consumers are not entitled to a refund under this recall. The remedy is limited to repair or replacement as described above.

---

**6. WHAT CONSUMERS SHOULD DO**

1. Locate the batch code on the rating plate on the rear lower panel of the heater.
2. If the batch code is listed in Section 1 of this notice, immediately stop using the heater and turn off the gas supply at the wall isolation valve.
3. Contact WarmGlow Pty Ltd to register for the free repair or replacement.

Contact details:

- **Telephone:** 1800 555 019 (free call, Monday to Friday, 8:30 am to 5:00 pm AEST)
- **Email:** recall@warmglow.com.au
- **Web:** www.warmglow.com.au/recall-2024-03

When contacting WarmGlow, please have the following information available:

- Batch code from the rating plate
- Date of purchase, if known
- Retailer where the unit was purchased, if known

WarmGlow Pty Ltd will arrange an appointment with a licensed gas fitter in the consumer's area. Appointments will be scheduled within 20 business days of registration.

---

**7. RETAILERS AND SUPPLIERS**

Retailers who have sold affected units should:

- Display a copy of this recall notice at the point of sale for a period of 60 days from the date of issue.

A list of known retailers who received affected stock is available from WarmGlow Pty Ltd on request.

**SECTION 6 – CONSUMER REMEDY OPTIONS**

This section explains the options available to you if you own an affected WarmGlow Model WG-2400 Heater. Please read this information carefully before contacting WarmGlow Pty Ltd.

**6.1 What you can choose**

Under the terms of this recall, you may choose either of the following remedies, at no cost to you:

- **Repair** – A qualified WarmGlow technician will replace the thermocouple assembly in your heater and carry out a functional test. The repair can be done in your home for most installations. If the heater cannot be repaired on site, WarmGlow will arrange collection and return it to you once the repair is complete.
- **Replacement** – If you prefer not to have the heater repaired, or if the unit cannot be safely repaired, WarmGlow will supply a replacement heater of equivalent value. The replacement model currently offered is the WarmGlow Model WG-2600, which has the same heating capacity and safety features. If the WG-2600 is not suitable for your needs, please contact WarmGlow to discuss alternatives.

**Important:** A refund is not available under this recall. The remedy is limited to repair or replacement as described above. This does not affect any rights you may have under the Australian Consumer Law.

**6.2 How to register for a remedy**

To arrange your remedy, you must register your heater with WarmGlow Pty Ltd. Registration is quick and can be done in one of three ways:

1. **Online** – Visit our recall registration page at www.warmglow.com.au/recall2024 and complete the online form. You will need your heater's model number (WG-2400) and batch code, which are printed on the rating label on the back of the unit.
2. **By phone** – Call our recall hotline on **1800 555 047** between 8:30 am and 5:00 pm (AEST), Monday to Friday. Our staff will take your details over the phone and book an appointment for you.
3. **By email** – Send an email to recall@warmglow.com.au with your name, contact number, address, and the batch code from your heater's rating label. We will respond within two business days.

**6.3 What happens after you register**

Once you have registered, WarmGlow will contact you to arrange a suitable time for the remedy. Please note the following:

- Appointments are scheduled within 20 business days of registration. As at the date of this notice, the average waiting time for an appointment is 16 business days.
- For repairs in the home, our technician will bring the replacement thermocouple assembly and all necessary tools. The repair takes approximately 30 minutes.
- If your heater needs to be collected for repair, WarmGlow will arrange a courier to pick it up from your address. The heater will be returned to you within 10 business days of collection.
- For replacements, the new heater will be delivered to your address. Our courier will take the old heater away at the time of delivery.

**6.4 Preparing for your appointment**

To help our technician complete the repair as quickly as possible, please:

- Make sure the heater is unplugged and cool before the technician arrives.
- Clear a space around the heater so the technician can access all sides of the unit.
- Have the heater's rating label visible if possible, so the technician can confirm the batch code.

**6.5 If you have already had the heater repaired**

If you have already had your heater repaired by a technician who was not authorised by WarmGlow, you may still be eligible for a remedy. Please contact the recall hotline and have your repair receipt available. We will assess each case individually.

If you do not have the original receipt, that is not a problem – the batch code on the rating label is sufficient for us to confirm whether your heater is affected.

If you have moved since purchasing your heater and have not yet registered, please use your current address when you register. WarmGlow will arrange for the repair or replacement to be carried out at the address you provide. If you have already registered and have since moved, please contact the recall hotline or email recall@warmglow.com.au with your updated details so we can ensure our records are correct.

---

**7. Where to find more information**

For further information about this recall, including the full list of affected batch codes, please visit the Product Safety Australia website at **www.productsafety.gov.au** and search for recall number **2024/12345**. The listing includes a copy of this notice, photographs of the affected heater model, and the full list of batch codes.

You can also find more information on the WarmGlow website at **www.warmglow.com.au/recall**. This page includes:

- A copy of this notice and any future revisions
- A list of frequently asked questions
- A short video showing how to locate the rating label on your heater
- A downloadable form you can print and post to us if you prefer not to register online, by phone, or by email

If you have any questions that are not answered by the information on these websites, please call the recall hotline on **1800 555 047** or send an email to **recall@warmglow.com.au**.

If you would like to receive updates about this recall by email or SMS, you can register for updates at **www.warmglow.com.au/recall/updates**. When you register for updates, we will send you:

- A confirmation when your remedy has been scheduled
- A reminder the day before your appointment
- A notification if there are any changes to the recall, such as an extension of the affected batch range or a change to the remedy

Please note that registering for updates is separate from registering your heater for the remedy. If you have already registered your heater using one of the methods in section 6.2, you will automatically receive updates by the same contact method you provided, and you do not need to register separately. If you would prefer to receive updates by a different method, please let our staff know when you register, or contact the recall hotline.

documents.content:
Product Safety Australia
Recall Notice 2024/12345 (Revision 3)
Issued 19 June 2024

**WarmGlow Ceramic Fan Heater — Model GHG-2000**
**Recall number: 2024/12345**
**Revision 3 — supersedes Revision 2 dated 12 June 2024**

This revision is issued to update the contact details for the remedy provider in Western Australia and to clarify the compliance status of replacement thermocouples used in repaired units. All other terms of the recall remain unchanged.

---

**1. Product description**

The recall affects the WarmGlow Ceramic Fan Heater, model GHG-2000, with a nominal power rating of 2000 W and a rated voltage of 220–240 V AC. The heater is a freestanding, fan-forced ceramic heater with a white body and a black control panel on the top rear of the unit. The model number and batch code are printed on the silver rating label affixed to the underside of the base.

Affected batch codes are:

GHG-2000-2301 through GHG-2000-2311 inclusive, and
GHG-2000-2401 through GHG-2000-2404 inclusive.

The batch code is a nine-character code printed on the rating label, for example, GHG-2000-2307. Only units with a batch code within the ranges listed above are affected. Units with a batch code outside these ranges are not affected by this recall.

Approximately 12,400 units with affected batch codes were sold in Australia between 1 January 2023 and 31 May 2024. The heaters were sold through major retailers including HomePlus Bayside, Coastal Electrical, and a number of independent hardware and home appliance stores, as well as through online marketplaces.

**2. Reason for the recall**

The heater has been found to present a risk of fire and burn injury due to a manufacturing defect in the thermal cutoff device. In affected units, the thermal cutoff may fail to operate correctly, allowing the heater to continue operating when the internal temperature exceeds the designed safe limit. This can cause the heater body to overheat, potentially resulting in the plastic housing melting or catching fire.

The defect was identified following a consumer incident reported to WarmGlow on 22 April 2024, in which a heater in a residential property in Bayside began to emit smoke and the rear panel showed signs of melting. The unit was returned to WarmGlow for examination, and testing confirmed that the thermal cutoff device had not activated at the required temperature. Subsequent testing of a sample of units from the same production batch identified the fault in a small proportion of units. The supplier of the thermal cutoff device has advised that a change in the calibration procedure at their factory in March 2023 may have resulted in a batch of devices with an incorrectly set trip temperature.

WarmGlow has received two further reports of heaters overheating, one in May 2024 and one in early June 2024. No injuries have been reported. The recall is being conducted in consultation with the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (the Commission).

**3. Hazards**

The main hazard associated with the affected heaters is fire. If the thermal cutoff device fails to operate, the heater can continue to heat beyond its design limits. The external surfaces of the heater can reach temperatures high enough to ignite nearby combustible materials or to cause burn injuries if touched. The heater may also emit smoke and an odour of burning plastic before the housing begins to melt.

Consumers are advised to stop using the heater immediately, unplug it from the power outlet, and not to use the heater again until it has been inspected and, if necessary, repaired or replaced under this recall.

documents.title: Recall Notice 2024-03
documents.content:
**4. What consumers should do**

Consumers who have purchased one of the affected WarmGlow WG-2000 panel heaters should immediately stop using the heater, unplug it from the power outlet, and contact WarmGlow to arrange a free replacement or refund.

To arrange a remedy, consumers can:

- Call WarmGlow’s dedicated recall hotline on 1800 634 227 (Monday to Friday, 9:00 am to 5:00 pm AEST).
- Email the recall team at recall@warmglow.com.au.
- Visit the WarmGlow website at www.warmglow.com.au/recall and complete the online recall form.

Consumers will need to provide their name, contact details, the model number and serial number from the rating label on the back of the heater, and proof of purchase if available. Proof of purchase is not required to receive a remedy, but it will help WarmGlow confirm the date and place of purchase.

WarmGlow will arrange for the affected heater to be collected from the consumer’s home at no cost, or will provide a prepaid return satchel for smaller items where collection is not practicable. Once the heater has been received and verified as an affected unit, WarmGlow will issue either a replacement heater of equivalent value or a full refund of the purchase price, at the consumer’s choice.

Consumers who purchased their heater from a retail store and prefer to return it in person may do so at the point of purchase. Participating retailers have been advised of the recall and will accept affected units. Consumers returning a heater to a store should bring their receipt if available, but the absence of a receipt will not prevent the return being processed.

Consumers who have registered their heater with WarmGlow for warranty purposes have been contacted directly by email or post with details of the recall. If you have not received a notification but believe your heater may be affected, please check the model and serial number against the list on the WarmGlow website or contact the recall hotline for assistance.

**5. Affected products and identification**

The recall affects the following product:

- Brand: WarmGlow
- Model: WG-2000
- Description: 2000W panel heater with digital thermostat, white finish
- Batch codes: 2023-03-01 through 2023-03-31 inclusive
- Serial number range: WG2000-30123-000001 through WG2000-30123-004800

The affected batch codes and serial number range are printed on the rating label located on the rear panel of the heater, near the power cord. The batch code is formatted as a date in the sequence YYYY-MM-DD. Consumers who have difficulty reading the rating label due to the position of the heater are advised to unplug the unit and, if necessary, lay it face down on a soft surface before attempting to read the label.

Units manufactured outside the batch code range listed above are not affected by this recall. Consumers who are unsure whether their unit is affected should contact the recall hotline for assistance, providing the batch code and serial number from the rating label.

**6. Remedy**

WarmGlow will provide a free replacement heater or a full refund of the purchase price for all affected units, regardless of the age of the heater and regardless of whether the consumer has proof of purchase. The consumer may choose which remedy they prefer. Replacement units are of the same model and specification, and have been manufactured with a corrected thermal cutoff device from a different supplier. The replacement units do not carry the defect described in this recall notice.

WG-2400 Sales Ledger – Summary to 31/05/2024
Prepared by: J. Whitfield (Inventory Coordinator)
Period covered: 15/08/2023 – 31/05/2024
Last updated: 31/05/2024 16:40

This summary consolidates all sales, adjustments, and stock movements for the WG-2400 model across the HomePlus Bayside store. It supersedes the interim summary circulated on 31/03/2024; that earlier document should be disregarded for any reporting purposes.

1. TOTAL SALES UNITS
Total units sold (incl. staff purchases) between 15/08/2023 and 31/05/2024: 1,847 units.
This figure includes 23 staff-discounted sales and 41 sales where the customer used a trade-in voucher. It does not include units returned by customers and later resold; those are counted at the point of the second sale.

Note: December 2023 includes 34 units sold in the pre-Christmas promotion week (18–24 Dec). January 2024 figure reflects the post-Christmas return period; 12 of the units sold that month were replacements for units returned under the 30-day change-of-mind policy.

3. RETURNS AND ADJUSTMENTS
Total customer returns recorded for the period: 87 units.
Of these:
– 52 were refunded in full (no fault found on inspection).
– 23 were exchanged for a new unit (fault confirmed on inspection).
– 9 were refunded after the customer reported the motor noise issue (all from batch 20230912).
– 3 were returned under the change-of-mind policy and resold within 14 days.

Return rate for the period: 4.7% of total sales. This is above the store average of 3.1% for similar small appliances. The elevated rate is attributed mainly to the batch 20230912 motor noise issue, which was identified in October 2023. A further review of return reasons is attached to the monthly stocktake file for May 2024.

4. STOCKTAKE VARIANCES
Four stocktake variances were recorded during the period:
– 30/11/2023: physical count 14, system 15 (variance -1). Unit 2400-9698 later located in the back dock area on 01/12/2023 and corrected.

– 31/03/2024: physical count 9, system 9 (no variance). No action required.
– 31/05/2024: physical count 4, system 4 (no variance). No action required.
